$comment: LEGAL CHARACTERISATION — A DIMENSION, NOT A LAYER.
MEASURE, INTERACTION and APPORTIONMENT ask what the ceiling refers to, how it meets other
exposure provisions, and among whom it operates. All three assume the clause IS a ceiling.
D4.29 produced a case where that assumption is the question. A cap measured on a payment class
that never arises computes to nil, and nil recovery is what an absolute bar produces. Whether
the clause is therefore a limitation or an exclusion is a legal characterisation, and it is not
answered by any of the three layers because it is prior to all of them.
It is recorded as a separate dimension so that it cannot be reached by arithmetic.
scope_of_this_record: The liability ceiling. It is NOT generalised to other clause families, because no evidence yet shows the problem recurs outside them — the same refusal recorded in cap-referent.json#engine_generalisation.

hard_constraint.constraint: A legal characterisation may never be inferred from a computed value. That the ceiling evaluates to zero does not make the clause an absolute bar, and that it evaluates to a positive figure does not make it a valid limitation.
why: The arithmetic is a fact about this instance. The characterisation is a question about the
clause, the parties, the bargaining relationship and the applicable authority, and Indian law
Inferring one from the other would let the engine author a legal conclusion out of a division
that happened to yield nil. It would also be unstable: the same clause between the same
parties would change legal character with the invoice history.
hard_constraint.consequence: The nil ceiling is surfaced as a computed fact and as an open characterisation question, never as a verdict.

characterisation_tree.$note: What the verified authorities actually distinguish. The branches are NOT mutually exclusive — a consumer contract can also contain an absolute bar — so this is a set of questions to be answered, not a classifier that returns one label.

branches.question: Is the restriction an absolute bar on claiming damages?
branches.reading: Held void under s.23 for negating ss.55 and 73.
branches.caution: A High Court decision on government standard terms with employer-caused delay. Its reach between commercial equals was not decided.

branches.question: Is it a threshold cap at a stated figure?
branches.reading: Enforceable, and enforceable even when very low.
branches.caution: The reasoning rests on what the signer could see on the page and the insurance route offered as an alternative. A formula offers neither.

branches.question: Is it an exclusion of a CATEGORY of loss?
branches.reading: Given effect where other heads remained available.
branches.caution: The judgment was not read; facts and holding come from a law report. Its relationship to Simplex is the practitioner literature's reading, not this court's words.

branches.question: Is the counterparty a consumer?
branches.authority: Consumer Protection Act 2019, s.2(46) with s.49(2)
branches.reading: A term unfair to a consumer may be declared null and void, on a statutory route that does not depend on the Simplex line at all.
branches.caution: Consumer status under the Act is itself fact-dependent and excludes acquisition for a commercial purpose. It cannot be read off a party type.

branches.question: Are the parties of comparable bargaining power?
branches.authority: Central Inland Water Transport v Brojo Nath Ganguly
branches.reading: Unconscionability may displace a term where there is great disparity and no meaningful choice.
branches.caution: Stated not to reach commercial transactions between equals. Transplanting it as a universal rule is the failure D4.28 recorded.

characterisation_tree.the_gap: Where the ceiling is a FORMULA whose referent can be zero, none of the branches answers it. It is textually a threshold, substantively a bar, and category-wise neither. No authority found addresses it.

$note: cap-referent.json records seven families whose ceiling is structurally empty. They share an
arithmetic and they do not share a legal position. Treating them as one population would
produce a rule that is wrong for at least two of them.

populations.character: Unilateral instruments published to an unnamed counterparty. Neither family collects party_2 at all — verified against the schemas.
populations.route: Consumer Protection Act 2019 s.2(46) / s.49(2), which is available regardless of how the Simplex line resolves.
populations.additional_question: Whether a published policy is a contract at all, and on what assent — already a live question elsewhere in this investigation.

populations.character: Negotiated bilateral instruments between named parties.
populations.route: Depends entirely on the Simplex / Bharathi Knitting characterisation, which is unsettled.
fact_sensitivity: NDA — routinely executed between a large company and an individual on the company's form. Whether bargaining power is comparable varies case by case and the instrument records nothing about it.
FOUNDERS_AGREEMENT — the parties are individuals, and disparity between a lead founder and a junior one is common. Also not recorded.

populations.character: A DPA sits alongside a services agreement. Fees are payable under the PRINCIPAL contract, not under the DPA, so its ceiling measures a payment that arises next door.
populations.route: Distinct from both populations above. Obligations under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 may fall within the clause's own carve-out for liabilities that cannot be limited by law, which would make the nil ceiling partly inoperative rather than total.
populations.status: the DPDP interaction is NOT established here and is recorded as a question

the_seven_are_not_one_population.consequence: A future rule cannot say "nil cap = invalid". It has to reach character of the restriction, contractual context, parties, bargaining relationship, consumer status, statutory route, applicable authority and the facts.

the_facts_are_not_collected.finding: The system cannot characterise, because it never asks. No family among the seven collects consumer status or anything describing the bargaining relationship — verified by scanning every field label, name and description in all seven schemas.
the_facts_are_not_collected.what_exists_instead: party_1_type and party_2_type, which record legal form — company, LLP, individual, partnership firm, trust, government body.

forbidden_inference.rule: Legal form must never be used to infer consumer status or bargaining relationship.
why: An individual counterparty is not necessarily a consumer: the Consumer Protection Act excludes acquisition for resale or a commercial purpose, so a sole proprietor buying for the business is not one.
A company counterparty is not necessarily an equal: a two-person private limited company signing a multinational's standard form is a company and is not of comparable bargaining power.
In TERMS_OF_SERVICE and PRIVACY_POLICY the only party type collected is the PUBLISHER's, which says nothing whatever about the reader.
forbidden_inference.$discipline: This is the convenient inference. It is available, it would let the engine produce a characterisation, and it would be an invention. Recorded as forbidden so that it is refused deliberately rather than never noticed.

the_facts_are_not_collected.consequence: The characterisation is not merely undecided. It is UNASKABLE on the present intake, and closing that gap is an intake and legal-model question, not a drafting one.

what_this_record_does_not_do: It does not decide whether any family's ceiling is a bar or a cap.
It does not resolve the INTERACTION layer, which remains blocked on measurement per head.
It does not resolve LIABILITY_CAP_APPORTIONMENT, which remains open and untouched.
It does not add a field, a clause or a validator. Nothing here has been implemented.
